headline: You're having a kid
body: A due date, and a company that doesn't run itself. Something about how you work has to give.

options.label: Delegate more at work
options.detail: Hand over real decisions to the team, starting now, before you have to.
options.storyHeadline: Became a parent, leaned on a stronger team
options.mentorHint: You trust your team more. You'll also find out exactly how ready they were, at the worst possible time to learn it.

options.label: Push even harder
options.detail: Work more, not less, to build a bigger cushion before the baby arrives.
options.storyHeadline: Became a parent, worked harder
options.mentorHint: Revenue keeps climbing. Nobody's tracking what pushing even harder costs somewhere else.

headline: A parent offers to invest
body: They believe in you completely, and they want to put part of their retirement savings into the company to prove it.

options.label: Accept the investment
options.detail: Take their money and the weight of losing it if this doesn't work.
options.storyHeadline: Took a parent's retirement savings as investment

options.label: Thank them and decline
options.detail: It's too risky for their retirement, whatever they say. Turn it down gently.
options.storyHeadline: Turned down family investment

headline: You had to move back home
body: Runway is tight enough that your own rent is the easiest thing left to cut. You move in with family to save it.

options.label: Lean into it
options.detail: Tell it as the bootstrap story it actually is, to yourself as much as anyone.
options.storyHeadline: Moved home to conserve cash, and made peace with it

options.label: Resent every day of it
options.detail: Save the same money, but let it eat at you that it's come to this.
options.storyHeadline: Moved home, felt like a failure

headline: A baby
body: You're going to be a parent in six months.

options.label: Take four months off
options.detail: The company drifts. You are happy.
options.storyHeadline: Took real parental leave

options.label: Take two weeks
options.detail: The company is fine. You miss things you won't get back.
options.storyHeadline: Took two weeks and went straight back

options.label: Bring the baby to the office
options.detail: Somehow this works.
options.storyHeadline: Brought the baby to the office

headline: Your partner gets an offer abroad
body: It's the job they always wanted. It's in another country.

options.label: Go with them, run the company remotely
options.detail: Output slips. The relationship is intact.
options.storyHeadline: Moved abroad to run the company remotely

options.label: Stay
options.detail: A real gamble on the relationship.
options.storyHeadline: Stayed behind when the offer came

gamble.winText: It was hard for a year. It held.

headline: A parent is ill
body: Your mother is not well and lives four hours away.

options.label: Go, for as long as it takes
options.detail: The company slows. You have no regrets.
options.storyHeadline: Went to be with a sick parent

options.label: Send money instead
options.detail: It isn't the same and you know it.
options.storyHeadline: Sent money instead of going

headline: Your oldest friend wants a job
body: They aren't qualified. They know you know.

options.label: Hire them
options.detail: This could go either way.
options.storyHeadline: Hired an old friend, against your better judgement

gamble.winText: They grew into it and stayed a decade.
gamble.loseText: You fired them within a year. The friendship never quite recovered.
gamble.loseStoryHeadline: The old-friend hire didn't work out

options.label: Say no honestly
options.detail: The friendship survives, awkwardly.
options.storyHeadline: Said no to hiring a friend

headline: You haven't slept properly in two years

options.label: Take three months off
options.detail: The company drifts. You come back functional.
options.storyHeadline: Took three months to recover

options.label: Hire someone to run the day-to-day
options.detail: Costs a real salary. You keep your health.
options.storyHeadline: Hired someone to run daily operations

options.label: Push through
options.detail: Thirty percent odds this ends badly within two years.
options.storyHeadline: Pushed through the exhaustion

headline: Your sibling wants to invest
body: They have savings. They believe in you completely, which is the problem.

options.label: Take it
options.detail: Cash in, and now family dinners are board meetings.
options.storyHeadline: Took investment from family
options.mentorHint: The cash is real. So is the fact that your sibling now has an opinion about the company forever.

options.label: Refuse
options.detail: They're hurt. You sleep fine.
options.storyHeadline: Turned down a sibling's investment
options.mentorHint: They're hurt today. That's the whole cost, and it doesn't show up on any spreadsheet.

options.label: Take it as a loan, not shares
options.detail: You owe them, but you keep every share.
options.storyHeadline: Took a loan from family instead of equity
options.mentorHint: You keep every share. You also owe family money whether or not the company ever pays you a salary.

headline: A wedding on launch day
body: Your best friend set the date a year ago. So did your biggest customer.

options.label: Go to the wedding
options.detail: The launch slips two weeks. Nothing bad happens.
options.storyHeadline: Chose the wedding over the launch
options.mentorHint: The launch slips two weeks. Nothing bad happens — you just won't know what those two weeks cost until later.

options.label: Skip it
options.detail: The customer is happy. The friendship quietly never recovers.
options.storyHeadline: Skipped the wedding for the launch
options.mentorHint: The customer's happy today. Some friendships don't announce they're over, they just quietly stop being what they were.

headline: Your kid says the company ruined their childhood
body: They're fifteen and they aren't being dramatic.

options.label: Step back properly
options.detail: Output drops. The relationship repairs.
options.storyHeadline: Stepped back to repair things at home

options.label: Explain why it mattered
options.detail: It doesn't land.
options.storyHeadline: Tried to explain why it mattered

headline: Someone to hand it to
body: Not just a kid. Someone who might actually want this, one day.

options.label: Start a family
options.detail: Real time away, real cost. Also, genuinely, the whole point.
options.storyHeadline: Started a family
options.mentorHint: Three years of slower growth is the honest price. Nobody prices the part where you're glad you did it.

options.label: Not now
options.detail: The company stays the only thing you're building.
options.storyHeadline: Decided against starting a family, for now
